description: Vendored copy of the house Renovate policy. The sibling repositories consume it as a shared preset; this one cannot — the preset lives in a private repository, and a public repo can neither name it (the leak scanner rejects private repo names, correctly) nor resolve it at Renovate runtime without credentials it will never have. Vendoring is the same call SPEC D3 already makes for the shared lint configs. Keep it in step by hand; the drift test belongs on the private side, which can name both repositories.

minimumReleaseAge holds every update for seven days after it is published. The window it closes is the one where a compromised version goes up and is yanked days later: a bot that upgrades within the hour installs it, and a bot that waits a week never sees it. The cost is seven days of latency on a patch that fixes something real, and that cost is accepted deliberately — a security advisory routes through vulnerabilityAlerts, which is exempt from this delay.

automerge below is only half a decision. platformAutomerge hands the merge to GitHub, where branch protection is the gate; with Allow auto-merge switched off in repository settings, Renovate falls back to merging through the API itself and the gate is whatever Renovate checked. The config and the repository setting have to agree, and only one of them is in this file.

schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: Automerge is OFF. It was on for patch and minor bumps, and on 2026-09-02 three of them merged themselves in one evening with nobody watching: #193 at 20:25:33Z, which split the bun version across managers, and #195 at 02:51:24Z, which merged while the repository's Allow auto-merge setting was already switched off. That second one is the fallback the third paragraph above predicts — with the platform gate unavailable Renovate merges through its own API, so switching the repository setting off changes who merges without changing whether merging happens. This key is the one that stops it. automergeType and platformAutomerge stay here and inert, because automerge defaults to false and both only take effect when it is true; leaving them makes re-enabling one boolean rather than a reconstruction. Renovate still opens, groups and rebases PRs — only the merge is withheld. When it was on, green meant the single required context, verify, which aggregates 18 jobs. That number is pinned by tools/check-claims.sh C9 and derived from ci.yml, because it sat at 17 here while the workflow had already grown past it — a description nothing reads is a description nothing corrects.
Majors are always a human decision.
React and its types move together or the JSX types desync.
Action digest bumps are noisy individually and identical in risk.

The compiler pin is never automerged. site/ is scheduled to move to TypeScript 7, where installing a package named typescript at 7.x silently retargets JS-API consumers — a change that can pass every gate while checking nothing.

Rust dependency changes stay human. The workspace pins its dependencies centrally and six crates sit outside default-members with their own CI jobs, so a cargo bump's blast radius is not visible from the diff. This rule does NOT cover the MSRV, though it claimed to until now, and that sentence is how the gap below stayed invisible: the MSRV pin is a `uses-with` input under the github-actions manager, not a cargo dependency, so this matcher never reached it.

The MSRV is declared once, in Cargo.toml rust-version, and restated on four other surfaces that tools/check-claims.sh C1 holds equal to it. Renovate can only ever move ONE of them — the `toolchain:` input this rule disables — so every such update is wrong by construction. It proposed 1.94 to 1.98 on #177, where the github-actions group above would have automerged it on green and left the msrv job compiling on a version the crates do not advertise; C1 going red is the only reason that did not happen. Raising the MSRV is a deliberate edit to all five surfaces at once, not a dependency bump.

The bun version is one claim restated on eight surfaces, and Renovate reaches them through four different managers, so no single bot PR can move all of them. Its own tool-constraint updater owns constraints.bun above; npm owns @types/bun in contracts/ and site/ and the packageManager field in site/package.json; the github-actions manager owns the three bun-version uses-with inputs in ci.yml; the dockerfile manager owns the two oven/bun image pins in site/Dockerfile. Each package name here is copied from Renovate's own PR tables — #193 listed bun as tool-constraint and as packageManager, and @types/bun as devDependencies; #177 listed bun as uses-with; and #197, which merged while this PR was open, listed node as final for this very Dockerfile, so the dockerfile manager is demonstrably active on that file and names a FROM by its image name — oven/bun is that same shape two stages up. An earlier revision of this caption called oven/bun inferred, on the grounds that Renovate had never proposed a change to site/Dockerfile. That was wrong twice over: it was checked against local refs rather than the forge, and #197 was already open when it was checked. #193 moved four of the eight to 1.4.0 and automerged unattended on green, leaving ci.yml and the Dockerfile at 1.3.14. Nothing went red, because a partial move of a claim that spans managers is invisible to any gate scoped to one of them. This rule therefore matches by package name rather than by manager, since the manager is the axis that splits the claim. Raising bun is a deliberate edit to all eight surfaces at once, including a fresh digest for the oven/bun image on the deployed site path, and it is not a dependency bump.
